items.title: Safety and accuracy diverge across deployment conditions in clinical large language models
items.excerpt: Scaling clinical LLMs by size, context, retrieval or inference compute raises accuracy but does not guarantee safety: the study finds confident, evidence-contradicting errors diverge from average accuracy across deployment conditions.
items.rationale: Directly actionable for health systems deploying LLMs: bigger models, retrieval or more compute raise accuracy without making the models safer, so safety has to be evaluated on its own. No earlier card made this accuracy-vs-safety argument.

items.title: DKI may improve care in mild newborn HIE cases
items.excerpt: A machine-learning model combining diffusion kurtosis MRI with clinical data predicted 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes in 740 newborns with mild HIE (external AUC 0.92) in a prospective four-hospital study published Nov 24 in Radiology.
items.rationale: Prospective four-hospital Radiology study with 740 newborns and external AUC 0.92. It targets a real treatment-decision gap in mild neonatal HIE, a new population for the section.

items.title: 식약처, AI·멀티오믹스로 의약품 부작용 예측한다
items.excerpt: 식약처 식품의약품안전평가원이 12월 4일 의약품 부작용·약물 반응성 예측 연구를 지원하는 AI·멀티오믹스 통합 데이터 플랫폼 'K-PREDICT' 시범운영에 들어가고, 2027년 7월 본격 운영한다.
items.rationale: Regulator-run AI platform for predicting drug side effects, with fixed dates: pilot on Dec 4, full operation in July 2027. It is a different system from the MFDS review-assist AI carded on 11-09.

items.title: AI technology helping local cancer patients access treatment faster
items.source: Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
items.excerpt: SaTH now uses the Limbus AI auto-contouring system for all radiotherapy treatment sites, saving about 10 hours of contouring per week and cutting the wait between referral and the start of radiotherapy.
items.rationale: Primary-source report of a real hospital rollout: AI auto-contouring now covers every radiotherapy site, saves about 10 hours a week and shortens the wait to treatment. Radiotherapy workflow has not appeared in the 30-day history.

items.title: AI-assisted chest CT scan analysis of body composition at ICU admission and 6-month mortality
items.excerpt: In a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort of 509 ICU patients, AI-automated chest CT body-composition measurement at admission was associated with 6-month mortality — a measure rarely taken in practice because manual CT analysis is labor-intensive.
items.rationale: Turns chest CTs already taken at ICU admission into a 6-month mortality signal (509-patient prospective cohort) by automating a measurement too labour-intensive to do by hand. This is a different question from the 11-18 PCCT image-quality item.

dedup.note: Dropped as duplicates or follow-ups: (1) 데일리팜 '심비(SIMBI)' 12월 2일 공개 (dailypharm 345117). It follows the 11-09 card (dailypharm 344134), which already reported the December reveal of the MFDS AI review-assist system. What is new is only a name and a launch date, and the launch has not happened, so it is held until the actual launch. (2) HTN SENTINEL-AI national NHS AI-performance monitoring (htn.co.uk). It is very likely the same running story as the 11-15 'NHS launches £200k project' monitoring card (publictechnology.net). Both are national frameworks for monitoring deployed diagnostic AI, and nothing in the excerpt shows a separate new decision. Skipped on judgement, not as duplicates: NEJM AI FDA-authorized sepsis tool (the brief says to skip it because of the erratum trap); Nature ORIDTP peptides (animal-stage only, and the pool was not short); Innovaccer Grok Voice (vendor integration promo, already skipped on 11-27 on the same grounds); Zimmer Monogram FDA submission (AI may be incidental to an autonomous-robot filing, and it comes from an off-list outlet); npj FeNetDP pancreatic ferroptosis repurposing (computational only, lower actionability). Diversity: 4 distinct outlets, and npj Digital Medicine has 2 picks, which is the cap. I could not grep published_urls.json across sections because I have no search tool. The 5 picks are clinical or regulator stories, so a cross-section clash is unlikely, but the orchestrator should still run its archive key-term scan (K-PREDICT, Limbus, DKI HIE).
